svg.title: P017 · Orders with payment type and shipper
svg.desc: One row per order in the latest seven calendar dates. Orders 1 and 2 both match UPI. Order 3 has a NULL payment ID. All three orders survive. Orders 1 and 2 match FastShip. The missing shipper on order 3 adds NULLs, so the working result still has three orders. Read Orders for the window bounds. December 31 minus six days is December 25. Both endpoints count. The date filter removes order 1 from the joined rows. December 25 (order 2) and December 31 (order 3) both qualify. Order 3 appears first with Unknown in both fields. Order 2 follows with UPI and FastShip. First · FROM Orders. The report needs an entry for each order in the date window, including orders with missing labels. Each order already carries both lookup IDs. Second · LEFT JOIN Payments. Look up Orders.PaymentID in Payments to get the payment type. A failed match leaves the order available for the shipper lookup. Third · LEFT JOIN Shippers. Match Orders.ShipperID to Shippers on the rows carried from step 1. A missing shipper leaves a NULL company name. Both lookups use separate order columns, so they can trade places. Reporting window · FROM Orders. The CTE reads order dates to produce one pair of bounds. The main query starts from individual orders because it needs one result per qualifying order.
svg.text: Orders with payment type and shipper
One row per order in the latest seven calendar dates.
Order 3 has neither lookup key. At which step could an INNER JOIN lose it?
A triangle marks an example to follow. Shaded columns show what to read. Double underlines mark the matching keys. SQL excerpts use … for

svg.text: Orders 1 and 2 both match UPI. Order 3 has a NULL payment ID. All three orders survive.
Orders LEFT JOIN Payments ON Orders.PaymentID = Payments.PaymentID
Why use a second left join for Shippers?

g.text: Match Orders.ShipperID to Shippers on the rows carried from step 1. A missing shipper leaves a NULL company name.
Both lookups use separate order columns, so they can trade places.
